title: Guild-wide cooldown sharing channel
quote: My raiders sit in the same guild but in different groups, and I want my officers to see what the other team has ready without joining their group.
what: An optional guild mode sends the same cooldown and ready messages over the guild channel. A small guild list shows who in the guild is online with the addon and which tracked spells are ready or on cooldown, so an officer can check the other raid team or the M+ crowd. It is off by default so it adds no guild chat traffic.
possible: Partly on Retail and WoW: Forever (only members who run the addon appear). On Era, TBC and MoP the combat log only covers your own group, so the same limit applies outside it.
today: Today: messages only go to INSTANCE_CHAT, RAID or PARTY (Comms.lua GroupChannel); nothing uses the guild channel

title: Guild roll call with old-version warning
quote: Half the guild is on an old version and I only find out when someone asks why they are missing from my raid.
what: A /cdc guild command asks everyone online in the guild to answer with their version and client. It lists who runs it, who is on an older version, and who never answered, so the GM can post a message to the guild. This differs from a version hello in the group because it covers guild members who are not in the party.
possible: Possible on every client (needs the guild addon channel; only members who run the addon answer)
today: Today: no version is sent in any message, and the guild channel is not used (Comms.lua)

title: Settings profiles with a guild default
quote: I want to hand every new member one setup so they stop asking me which spells to untick.
what: Settings can be saved as named profiles, and a character picks which profile to use. Alts can follow the main's profile, or each class can get its own. The GM can also set a guild default that other members accept with one click.
today: Today: one account-wide CooldownCollaboratorDB with a single set of options and disabledSpells; no profiles and no per-character settings (CooldownCollaborator.lua Init)

title: Officer-pushed guild setup
quote: When we change our raid plan I want to send the new spell list to everyone once, not paste instructions in Discord.
what: The guild leader or an officer pushes a spell list and a few options (which spells to track, minimum duration, show ready) over the guild channel. Members get a prompt: Accept, Not now, or Never from this person. Nothing changes unless the member accepts, and they can revert.
possible: Possible on every client for members who run the addon; the spell list stays per client because each client tracks different spells
today: Today: spells and custom spells are only edited by hand in each player's own Settings; the only messages received are cooldown, ready and flask/food ones

title: Alts share settings, with a per-character override
quote: My members switch between a main and four alts all week, and I do not want each alt to start from a blank panel.
what: Positions, scale and other options carry across all characters by default, with a per-character override for the ones that differ (a healer alt that wants the panel somewhere else). The roster also remembers that a group member's character belongs to a known player, so a swap mid-raid does not leave a stale row behind.
possible: Possible on every client for your own settings; linking someone else's alts is Partly (only via addon messages or the guild roster)
today: Today: one account-wide DB, and roster state is keyed by character name and realm (CooldownCollaborator.lua FullName) with no link between alts

title: First-run note for new members
quote: A new recruit installs it and sees nothing until they join a group, then they ask me what is wrong.
what: On the first load the addon prints a short note and opens the settings once. It says the panel only appears in a group, shows the two settings worth checking, and tells Retail and Forever players that their groupmates need the addon too. A copyable one-line message the GM can paste into guild chat is included.
today: Today: no first-run note; the panel, Essentials bar and lanes stay hidden until you join a group (Lanes.lua, Essentials.lua)

title: Raid-team player filter
quote: I run three raid teams and an M+ crowd, and I only care about the team on the pull right now.
what: Pick a named team (a set of player names) and the panel, Essentials bar and lanes show only those players while the filter is on. People outside the team are hidden, not removed, so switching back is one click. Teams can be saved and shared between officers.
possible: Possible on every client (it hides known rows; it cannot reveal players the game hides on Retail and Forever)
today: Today: every known group member is shown; there is no per-player filter (UI.lua, Roster.lua)

title: Support summary for a member's problem
quote: When someone says it does not work, I want one block of text they can paste to me instead of five questions.
what: A /cdc support command prints a short copyable summary: addon version, client, group type, which groupmates have been seen sending messages, which spells are unticked, and the last send errors. The GM pastes it into a ticket or sends it to the author.
today: Today: /cdc debug prints cooldowns and group state to chat and /cdc verbose logs live; there is no single summary to copy (CooldownCollaborator.lua slash handler)
